description: Eight tables the four bundled packs know nothing about, at the width the add-on or Sentinel actually lands them (33 to 63 columns), with discovery-shaped profiles (top values with counts, numeric and dynamic flags). tools/dev/check-bindings.mjs and tests/propose.test.js assert the proposer does not recognise any of them as a feed: a CIM-normalised firewall log, a CIM-normalised Zeek log, an Okta System Log, an Entra AuditLogs table, a Windows SecurityEvent table, an Azure Activity table, a flattened GuardDuty finding and a generic application log. Every Splunk table carries the default fields host, source, sourcetype and index.

tables.note: A CIM-normalised firewall sourcetype (Palo Alto traffic log as its add-on lands it): src/dest/action/user/app/bytes and the vendor fields underneath, plus the Splunk default fields.
Zeek conn.log as Splunk_TA_zeek lands it, CIM-normalised (src/dest/action/app/bytes) on top of the raw id.orig_h fields.
Okta System Log as its own add-on indexes it: dotted actor/client/outcome/target objects, nothing bound in any pack.

top.value: User single sign on to app
User single sign on to app

tables.note: Windows Security 4624/4625 in Sentinel's SecurityEvent table: EventID, Computer, Account, SIDs, logon ids, the Sentinel system columns.

top.value: 4624 - An account was successfully logged on.
4625 - An account failed to log on.

tables.note: Entra's own audit table, not the sign-in log the entra-signin pack knows: same tenant, same Azure common schema, a different feed. InitiatedBy and TargetResources are dynamic.
Azure Activity log: the Azure Monitor common schema (OperationName, CorrelationId, CallerIpAddress, Level, Category, Properties) that every diagnostics table shares with SigninLogs.

A GuardDuty finding as Splunk_TA_aws flattens it: accountId, arn, region, resource.* and service.* paths, plus the CIM fields (src_ip, user, signature, category, vendor_account) the add-on stamps on every AWS sourcetype.

tables.note: A custom application log with the generic names an app team picks (user, user_id, ip, method, request_id, session_id, account_id, version, host, source) and the Splunk default fields.
